thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Routing anomaly detected — p99 request latency for streaming endpoints in eu-west-1 climbed from ~220ms to ~2.1s in the last 6m. Alert: routing.p99 > 1s for 5m
meera: paging the oncall, taking live. I see tail spikes aligned with routing weight churn around 00:42 UTC.
ben: oncall here. confirming customer-facing errors? any 5xx?
laura-cs: got a DM from a customer in fintech EU complaining about stream stalls and partial outputs — no 5xx but many client timeouts at 30s.
kai: digging into router metrics — there are >30% of streams routed to a small set of backends (hotset). p95 looks ok, p99 huge. bucketed by origin region shows skew toward a single shard group: shard-zu4.
meera: that smells like a policy weighting inversion. Did the recent rollout to routing-policy v2 land in eu-west?
alex: yes we rolled policy-v2 at 00:30 in eu-west. It included a weight normalization change. Rollout was gradual 10->50->100%.
ben: can we confirm correlation? overlay rollout percentage timeline with p99 timeline.
kai: attaching quick snippet of the query I ran:
```
SELECT time, routing_rollout_pct, p99_latency_ms
FROM telemetry.router_metrics
WHERE region='eu-west-1'
AND metric in ('p99_latency_ms','routing_rollout_pct')
ORDER BY time desc
LIMIT 200
```
alex: timeline lines up — p99 jumps after rollout reached ~60%.
meera: action plan: 1) pause/rollback policy-v2 in eu-west 2) divert new streaming sessions away from shard-zu4 while we triage 3) notify customers and start postmortem.
ben: I'll pause the rollout now. triggering rollback to policy-v1 for eu-west.
oncall-bot: ben requested a rollout rollback: policy-v2 -> policy-v1 in eu-west. ETA 30s.
sre-ops: running quick health probe on shard-zu4 — CPU nice but connection queue depth is high (100+), and KV cache miss ratio spiked. Could be routing producing concentrated tail load.
ben: rollback complete. verifying routing map... looks like traffic redistributed across more shards.
kai: p99 trending down from 2100ms -> 420ms within 90s. p95 steady ~180-240ms.
laura-cs: informing impacted customer that we observed an issue and rolled back a routing change; next update in 30m.
meera: temporary mitigation: add a soft-shed threshold to router for per-shard inflight > 60 to avoid re-concentrating. Can someone push a safe circuit-breaker?
\alex: I can push a transient heuristic change — add reject-bias for shards with inflight>60 for 10m. pushing now.
alex: pushed heuristic change to eu-west. monitor for re-concentration.
kai: after heuristic push, shard-zu4 inflight dropped to 28 and p99 down to ~300ms.
ben: routing logs show many sessions that hit shard-zu4 had long tail due to prefix cache churn — those were mostly large context streams.
meera: root hypotheses: a) policy-v2 normalization exposed weight skew where a small number of high-capacity model routes got increased affinity to shard-zu4 b) shard-level cache pressure (KV/prefix cache) amplified tail latency for sessions hitting that shard c) heuristic and rollback mitigated but we need fix.
laura-cs: CS asked for ETA to ensure SLA — customers want assurance. Should we open an incident page and notif external SLA owners?
meera: yes, mark this P1 incident. I'll open the incident doc.
meera: taking action items on triage: create a reproducer for policy normalization on staging, run simulated streaming workloads to verify weight distribution, and add a unit test for rollout gating when shard concentration > x%.
ben: ops follow-ups: schedule a shard cache sizing evaluation and add alert when shard inflight > 50 for >3m.
alex: engineering follow-ups: revert weight normalization change in our codebase pending more robust rollout gating.
kai: telemetry follow-ups: add route-level breakouts for streaming sessions by model size and context length so we can correlate cache churn.
sre-ops: will scrub logs for any backend errors during the window and synthesize a timeline for the postmortem.
laura-cs: customer update sent — "We observed routing-related tail latency after a configuration rollout; mitigations applied (rollback + soft-shed); investigating; will follow up with RCA within 48h."
meera: handoff to night oncall in 30m — ben stays for 15m overlap, then send a short summary in #incidents and hand to @kai as follow-up lead overnight.
ben: summary for handoff: rolled back routing-policy v2 in eu-west at 00:44 UTC -> immediate p99 improvement; applied per-shard inflight soft-shed; primary suspect: weight normalization + cache pressure causing hot-concentration. Follow-ups assigned to eng (alex), infra (sre-ops), telemetry (kai), CS (laura-cs).
oncall-bot: ben marked incident as acknowledged and assigned follow-ups.
meera: adding that customer impact: 3 customers reported degraded streaming quality; estimated affected sessions ~0.6% of regional traffic during window. No data leak or 5xx.
kai: will own overnight monitoring and postmortem draft. I'll ping in morning with timeline and logs.
laura-cs: I'll coordinate with account teams for direct outreach tomorrow.
ben: thanks all. if anything regresses, re-ping me with :pager: and I'll rejoin.
meera: closing live mitigation loop for now. filing incident P1 and tagging for RCA. :white_check_mark:
